entities.name: Centralized Architecture
entities.definition: A database system architecture that runs on a centralized server machine.

entities.name: Shared Memory Server Architecture
entities.definition: A database system architecture that uses multiple CPUs and exploits parallel processing, with all CPUs accessing a common shared memory.

entities.name: Parallel Databases
entities.definition: Databases designed to run on a cluster consisting of multiple machines.

entities.name: Distributed Databases
entities.definition: Databases that allow data storage and query processing across multiple geographically separated machines.

entities.name: Two-Tier Architecture
entities.definition: A database application architecture where the application resides at the client machine and invokes database system functionality at the server machine through query language statements.

The centralized architecture shown in Figure 1.3 is applicable to shared-memory server architectures, which have multiple CPUs and exploit parallel processing, but all the CPUs access a common shared memory.
To scale up to even larger data volumes and even higher processing speeds, parallel databases are designed to run on a cluster consisting of multiple machines.

Earlier-generation database applications used a two-tier architecture, where the application resides at the client machine, and invokes database system functionality at the server machine through query language statements.
